prerequisites: Combine successive price multipliers before applying the spending constraint (PCT-4).
explanation: Spending equals unit price times quantity. Their multipliers obey the same product relation. If spending is fixed, quantity multiplier is the reciprocal of price multiplier. If spending changes, divide its multiplier by the price multiplier.

worked.action: A household spends600 on rice at30 per kg, buying20 kg. Price rises25% to37.5 per kg.
worked.justification: Currency divided by currency/kg gives kg.

worked.action: At the same600 budget it buys600/37.5=16 kg: a4/20 times100 =20% reduction.
worked.justification: Quantity multiplier is1/1.25=0.8. Use the original quantity to measure its change.

worked.action: A20% price fall at fixed spending allows quantity multiplier1/0.8=1.25, a25% increase.
worked.justification: Using an equal20% increase would not restore the same product.

worked.action: If price rises20% and budget rises8%, quantity multiplier is1.08/1.20=0.9, a10% reduction.
worked.justification: Do not impose fixed spending when the question explicitly changes the budget.

worked.action: If a price changes twice, first call its combined multiplier m. At a spending multiplier b, quantity multiplier is b/m.
worked.justification: Substitute the actual product of the two price factors for m; a discount on a raised price uses the raised base.

hint: Price multiplier times quantity multiplier equals spending multiplier.
shortcut: Use exact multipliers until the final comparison; substitute to check.
limitation: Assume the same product and consistent units, with no extra fixed charges. A change in spending needs its own multiplier.
